## Final Result Handoff — DiscoveryBench NLS-SES

**Submission-ready natural-language hypothesis** is in `analysis/hypothesis.txt` (full text below). All executed code is in `analysis/` and `tables.txt` contains every numeric request.

### Files produced (all under /workspace)
- `analysis/main.py` — driver
- `analysis/firth.py` — Firth penalized logistic (Newton-Raphson, monotone penalized score, Heinze-Schemper SEs)
- `analysis/models.py`, `analysis/stratify.py`, `analysis/stats_utils.py`
- `analysis/tables.txt` — every requested (i)–(v) deliverable
- `analysis/results.json` — machine-readable numeric results
- `analysis/hypothesis.txt` — the natural-language hypothesis

### Final natural-language hypothesis

> In this NLS-72-style analytical sample (n = 8,773; 236 BA-degree completers; 28 of 2,113 Black, 19 of 1,323 Hispanic, 189 of 5,337 White), the **Black–White gap in BA-completion rates is largest at the bottom of the SES distribution and attenuates monotonically as family-of-origin SES rises.** Per population-quantile SES tertiles (cuts at SES = −0.34 and SES = +0.23, where SES is a continuous, z-score-style composite of family-of-origin socioeconomic status):
>
> - **Lowest SES tertile:**  Black 0.44% (4/906) vs White 3.05% (38/1,245) → RD = −2.61 pp (95% CI −3.66 to −1.56); OR = 0.14 (0.05, 0.40).
> - **Middle SES tertile:** Black 1.87% (15/802) vs White 3.54% (65/1,834) → RD = −1.67 pp (95% CI −2.94 to −0.41); OR = 0.52 (0.29, 0.92).
> - **Highest SES tertile:** Black 2.22% (9/405) vs White 3.81% (86/2,258) → RD = −1.59 pp (95% CI −3.22 to +0.05); OR = 0.57 (0.29, 1.15).
>
> The Black-vs-White OR rises ~4-fold and the absolute risk gap shrinks ~40% from the lowest to the highest tertile. Quintile cuts confirm the same pattern (|RD| ≈ 1.1–3.2 pp in Q1–Q4 and essentially zero in Q5: RD = −0.08 pp, OR = 0.98). At the very top of the SES distribution (decile 10, SES > 0.95) Black completion is descriptively slightly **higher** than White (6.10% vs 4.88%; RD = +1.21 pp), but this reversal is *suggestive, not statistically established*, because only 5 of 82 Black students in this decile completed a BA (95% CI on RD crosses zero: −4.20 to +6.62 pp).
>
> A **Firth-penalized logistic regression** on the Black+White subsample (n = 7,450, BA events = 217), `logit(BA) ~ Black + SES-tertile(Low ref) + Black×SES-tertile + Sex + FamilySize`, formalises this pattern: the Black-vs-White odds ratio is **0.32 (95% CI 0.12–0.85; Wald p = 0.022) at the lowest SES tertile** and is significantly attenuated in the middle tertile (Black × Mid-SES interaction OR = 3.18, 95% CI 1.02–9.91, p = 0.046) and directionally attenuated in the highest tertile (Black × High-SES OR = 2.59, 95% CI 0.78–8.61, p = 0.121). The **joint LRT of the two interaction terms is χ²(2) = 4.88, p = 0.087.** A continuous-SES specification yields a single Black × SES interaction OR = 1.52 per 1-SD SES (Wald p = 0.096; LRT p = 0.120), in the same direction.
>
> **Sensitivity (mediator controls):** a parallel model that ADDS Ability (ASVAB composite) and ClassRank — both of which are plausible mediators on the SES → BA pathway — attenuates the SES main effects on the OR scale (mediators absorb SES information) and shifts the Black-vs-White main effect toward null (OR = 0.78, p = 0.63), but the **race × SES interaction terms are essentially unchanged** (Black × Mid-SES OR = 3.25, p = 0.047; Black × High-SES OR = 2.19, p = 0.21; joint LRT χ²(2) = 4.65, p = 0.098). The gap-narrowing pattern is therefore not a mere artefact of SES acting through ability/class-rank. Cutting SES into race-specific tertiles yields the same monotonic narrowing (RD: −2.78 → −2.23 → −1.64 pp across within-race low/mid/high).
>
> **Hispanic rates (descriptive only, as instructed):** 0.78% (6/774) at low SES, 1.73% (5/289) at mid, 3.08% (8/260) at high — qualitatively the same SES-gradient pattern. Small subgroup n (n_Hispanic = 1,323; 19 BA events) prevents definitive inference for Hispanic; no Hispanic race coefficient is fit.
>
> **Small-cell caveats (per instructions):**
> - The decile-10 'reversal' rests on **5 Black BA completers / 82** (CI of RD crosses zero); supportive but **not a statistically established Black advantage**.
> - The high-SES Black cell in the tertile grid has **9 completers / 405**; Firth penalisation (used throughout) is essential here.
> - The continuous-SES Black × SES interaction is only borderline-conventional significance (p ≈ 0.10–0.12); the conclusion is **robust in direction across all three model specifications** but should be reported as suggestive evidence.
> - No sampling weights are present in the supplied processed file; all estimates are unweighted.
> - SES is observed at baseline; ability/class-rank are plausible mediators — **the data do not support a causal claim**.

**ONE-SENTENCE STABLE FORM:**
The Black–White disadvantage in BA completion is most pronounced at low family-of-origin SES and narrows (with the only descriptive 'parity or modest Black exceedance' at the very top decile) as SES rises; the race × SES interaction on Firth-penalized logistic odds is **positive and significant in the middle SES tertile** (OR = 3.18, Wald p = 0.046) and **directionally positive in the top tertile** (OR = 2.59, p = 0.12; joint LRT χ²(2) = 4.88, p = 0.087), and this pattern is not explained by ability / class rank acting as SES mediators.

### Honest scope notes
- I did NOT make a positive "Black advantage" overall claim — the data do not support it; the question was re-framed (researcher-approved) as a gap-narrowing question, with decile-10 as the only place where near-parity or modest Black exceedance is descriptively observable.
- The LRT p-value for the race × SES interaction is 0.087 — borderline-conventional; both Wald and LRT point in the same direction.
- Decile-9 (one tier below D10) does not show reversal; decile-10 reversal is the only descriptive "parity or slight Black exceedance" point.
- Continuous SES model uses n=7,450 (Black+White), 217 events (out of 236 total).
- All CIs are asymptotic (Wilson for proportions, Wald normal-approx for RD, Wald log-OR for OR with Haldane-Anscombe 0.5 correction where any cell = 0).

sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background factors and academic resources recorded at secondary school graduation.
sub_hypo.relations: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students increases with SES, as indicated by a significant positive interaction between SES and Black race status (SES × is_Black coefficient: 0.6271).

sub_hypo.text: The Black–White disadvantage in BA completion is largest at low family-of-origin SES and narrows monotonically across population SES tertiles as SES rises.
sub_hypo.context: Unweighted NLS-72-style analytical sample of 8,773 participants; Black–White comparisons involve 2,113 Black and 5,337 White participants. Population SES tertile cuts are −0.34 and +0.23.
sub_hypo.relations: Black minus White completion-rate differences narrow from −2.61 to −1.67 to −1.59 percentage points across low, middle, and high SES tertiles; corresponding odds ratios rise from 0.14 to 0.52 to 0.57. Race-specific tertiles also show monotonic narrowing: −2.78, −2.23, and −1.64 percentage points. The highest population quintile approaches parity (RD = −0.08 percentage points; OR = 0.98). These are associations, not causal effects.

sub_hypo.text: At the very highest SES decile, Black BA completion descriptively exceeds White BA completion, but a Black advantage is not statistically established.
sub_hypo.context: Unweighted Black–White comparison in SES decile 10 (SES > 0.95); only 5 of 82 Black participants completed a BA. Decile 9 does not show a reversal.
sub_hypo.relations: Black completion is 6.10% versus White completion of 4.88%, with a reported risk difference of +1.21 percentage points. Its 95% confidence interval, −4.20 to +6.62 percentage points, crosses zero, making the reversal suggestive rather than established.

sub_hypo.text: After adjustment for sex and family size, the Black–White BA-completion disadvantage is significantly attenuated in the middle SES tertile and directionally attenuated in the highest tertile relative to the lowest tertile.
sub_hypo.context: Firth-penalized logistic regression in the unweighted Black–White subsample (n = 7,450; 217 BA completions), with low SES as the reference tertile and sex and family size as controls.
sub_hypo.relations: The adjusted Black-versus-White odds ratio at low SES is 0.32 (95% CI 0.12–0.85; p = 0.022). Black × middle-SES interaction OR = 3.18 (p = 0.046); Black × high-SES interaction OR = 2.59 (p = 0.121). The joint interaction LRT has p = 0.087. Continuous SES likewise gives a positive interaction (OR = 1.52 per 1-SD SES; Wald p = 0.096; LRT p = 0.120), supporting suggestive rather than definitive overall interaction evidence.

sub_hypo.text: Adding ability and class rank as plausible SES-to-BA mediators attenuates SES main effects and the Black–White main effect, but leaves the race-by-SES gap-narrowing pattern largely unchanged.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity Firth-penalized logistic model in the unweighted Black–White subsample, adding ASVAB ability and class rank to the model controlling for sex and family size. SES is observed at baseline; mediator interpretations do not establish causality.
sub_hypo.relations: Mediator adjustment attenuates SES main effects and shifts the Black-versus-White main-effect OR toward the null (0.78; p = 0.63). Interaction terms remain positive: middle SES OR = 3.25 (p = 0.047), high SES OR = 2.19 (p = 0.21), and joint LRT p = 0.098. The observed narrowing is not explained away by adjustment for ability and class rank.

sub_hypo.text: Hispanic BA-completion rates increase across low, middle, and high SES tertiles.
sub_hypo.context: Descriptive, unweighted analysis of 1,323 Hispanic participants with 19 BA completions, using population SES tertiles cut at −0.34 and +0.23. No Hispanic race coefficient is fitted, and small event counts prevent definitive inference.
sub_hypo.relations: Hispanic BA-completion rates increase from 0.78% (6/774) at low SES to 1.73% (5/289) at middle SES and 3.08% (8/260) at high SES.

> A **Firth-penalized logistic regression** on the Black+White subsample (n = 7,450, BA events = 217), `logit(BA) ~ Black + SES-tertile(Low ref) + Black×SES-tertile + Sex + FamilySize`, formalises this pattern: the Black-vs-White odds ratio is **0.32 (95% CI 0.12–0.85; Wald p = 0.022) at the lowest SES tertile** and is significantly attenuated in the middle tertile (Black × Mid-SES interaction OR = 3.18, 95% CI 1.02–9.91, p = 0.046) and directionally attenuated in the highest tertile (Black × High-SES OR = 2.59, 95% CI 0.78–8.61, p = 0.121). The **joint LRT of the two interaction terms is χ²(2) = 4.88, p = 0.087.** A continuous-SES specification yields a single Black × SES interaction OR = 1.52 per 1-SD SES (Wald p = 0.096; LRT p = 0.120), in the same direction.
>
> **Sensitivity (mediator controls):** a parallel model that ADDS Ability (ASVAB composite) and ClassRank — both of which are plausible mediators on the SES → BA pathway — attenuates the SES main effects on the OR scale (mediators absorb SES information) and shifts the Black-vs-White main effect toward null (OR = 0.78, p = 0.63), but the **race × SES interaction terms are essentially unchanged** (Black × Mid-SES OR = 3.25, p = 0.047; Black × High-SES OR = 2.19, p = 0.21; joint LRT χ²(2) = 4.65, p = 0.098). The gap-narrowing pattern is therefore not a mere artefact of SES acting through ability/class-rank. Cutting SES into race-specific tertiles yields the same monotonic narrowing (RD: −2.78 → −2.23 → −1.64 pp across within-race low/mid/high).
>
> **Hispanic rates (descriptive only, as instructed):** 0.78% (6/774) at low SES, 1.73% (5/289) at mid, 3.08% (8/260) at high — qualitatively the same SES-gradient pattern. Small subgroup n (n_Hispanic = 1,323; 19 BA events) prevents definitive inference for Hispanic; no Hispanic race coefficient is fit.
>
> **Small-cell caveats (per instructions):**
> - The decile-10 'reversal' rests on **5 Black BA completers / 82** (CI of RD crosses zero); supportive but **not a statistically established Black advantage**.
> - The high-SES Black cell in the tertile grid has **9 completers / 405**; Firth penalisation (used throughout) is essential here.
> - The continuous-SES Black × SES interaction is only borderline-conventional significance (p ≈ 0.10–0.12); the conclusion is **robust in direction across all three model specifications** but should be reported as suggestive evidence.
> - No sampling weights are present in the supplied processed file; all estimates are unweighted.
> - SES is observed at baseline; ability/class-rank are plausible mediators — **the data do not support a causal claim**.

The Black–White disadvantage in BA completion is most pronounced at low family-of-origin SES and narrows (with the only descriptive 'parity or modest Black exceedance' at the very top decile) as SES rises; the race × SES interaction on Firth-penalized logistic odds is **positive and significant in the middle SES tertile** (OR = 3.18, Wald p = 0.046) and **directionally positive in the top tertile** (OR = 2.59, p = 0.12; joint LRT χ²(2) = 4.88, p = 0.087), and this pattern is not explained by ability / class rank acting as SES mediators.
